quantContext.note: From this project's own scoring pipeline (companies.json + screener.js, Phases 1-5/7), included for reference only - not itself a research source.

whyCheapBearCase.answer: IBM's stock has fallen 19.7% over six months despite a reasonable P/E (20.98) and strong ROE (30.75%) [source: 1], and the Q2 FY2026 10-Q gives a direct, filing-sourced explanation: management states plainly that 'our second-quarter performance was below our expectations' [source: 2]. The specific cause is disclosed in detail - Infrastructure segment revenue fell 7.4% year-over-year, driven by a shortfall in the IBM Z mainframe program and associated software: 'In the final weeks of June, we saw a shift in client spending priorities that resulted in numerous large deals failing to close within the expected timelines,' with clients redirecting spending toward servers/storage/memory to secure supply ahead of expected price increases [source: 2]. This is a real, quantified, filing-disclosed operating miss - not merely macro sentiment. Gross margin also declined 1.0 point year-over-year to 57.7%, and pre-tax margin fell 0.9 points to 14.4% [source: 2]. Elevated leverage (debt/equity 2.246) [source: 1] compounds the concern, though the 10-Q shows this did not prevent income from continuing operations growing 4.1% over the first six months of 2026 [source: 2].

revenueEpsTrend.answer: Mixed by period. Q2 FY2026 revenue was $17,162 million versus $16,977 million in Q2 FY2025, up 1.1% (also 1.1% at constant currency, per the filing's own reconciliation) [source: 2, 6]. However, Q2 FY2026 net income was $2,165 million versus $2,194 million in Q2 FY2025, down 1.3%, and GAAP diluted EPS from continuing operations was $2.27 versus $2.31, down 1.7% [source: 2, 6]. Looking at the first six months, the trend reverses to improving: H1 FY2026 revenue was $33,079 million versus $31,519 million in H1 FY2025, up 5.0% reported; net income was $3,381 million versus $3,249 million, up 4.1%; and diluted EPS was $3.55 versus $3.43, up 3.5% [source: 2, 6]. Operating (non-GAAP) earnings, which exclude acquisition-related charges and non-operating retirement costs, grew faster than GAAP in both periods: Q2 operating EPS $2.93 vs $2.80 (+4.6%), H1 operating EPS $4.84 vs $4.40 (+10.0%) [source: 2]. For context, full-year FY2025 (10-K, via XBRL) showed revenue of $67,535 million and net income of $10,593 million with diluted EPS of $11.17 [source: 6]. The net effect: Q2 alone was a GAAP earnings miss concentrated in Infrastructure/mainframe timing, but the H1 trend and the non-GAAP operating trend are both still positive.

marginTrend.answer: Compressing in Q2 FY2026 on a GAAP basis, though less so on an operating (non-GAAP) basis. GAAP gross profit margin fell 1.0 percentage point year-over-year to 57.7% in Q2 FY2026, and income-from-continuing-operations margin fell 0.3 points to 12.6%; pre-tax margin fell 0.9 points to 14.4% [source: 2]. Management attributes the gross margin decline to 'our revenue shortfall and mix, partially offset by productivity actions' [source: 2]. On an operating (non-GAAP) basis the picture is better: operating gross margin fell a smaller 0.7 points to 59.4%, and operating pre-tax margin from continuing operations actually rose 0.3 points to 19.2%, with operating net income margin up 0.6 points to 16.3% [source: 2]. Segment detail: 'Software and Consulting segment profit margins improved year to year, while Infrastructure profit margin was impacted by the IBM Z shortfall and cycle dynamics' [source: 2] - so the margin compression is concentrated in one segment (Infrastructure/mainframe), not company-wide.

guidanceChange.answer: Not determinable with a specific figure from the extracted filing text. The MD&A excerpt captured for this pass is truncated right after management states the H1 revenue and net income totals, and does not include an explicit full-year guidance range in the available text [source: 2]. However, management's own characterization that 'our second-quarter performance was below our expectations' [source: 2] is itself a direct, filing-sourced admission of an internal miss versus their own prior expectations, even though no specific revised numeric guidance was captured in this extract. None of the cached news headlines for IBM discuss guidance specifically.

catalysts.text: Software segment strength: Software revenue grew 5.1% as reported (4.6% at constant currency) in Q2 FY2026, and management notes 'about 80 percent of our software revenue is recurring in nature and delivered healthy growth in the quarter' - a structurally favorable revenue-mix shift if it continues.

Distributed Infrastructure revenue increased 37% in Q2 FY2026, 'our strongest quarter on record,' as clients redirected spending toward servers/storage/memory ahead of expected price increases - a demand pull-forward that could partially offset the mainframe (IBM Z) shortfall in future periods.

A new acquisition was signed July 22, 2026 (business not named in the extracted text), expected to close in the second half of 2026 subject to regulatory approval, to be integrated into the Infrastructure segment - a concrete, dated, near-term inorganic growth catalyst.

risks.text: IBM Z mainframe program shortfall: management explicitly disclosed that 'numerous large deals fail[ed] to close within the expected timelines' in the final weeks of Q2 FY2026, driving the majority of the quarter's revenue miss - a real, filing-documented demand-timing risk that could recur in future quarters if deal cycles remain elongated.

Elevated leverage: debt/equity of 2.246 per this project's own SEC-XBRL-based calculation, high even for a large-cap technology company, which increases sensitivity to any further earnings shortfalls.

Ordinary-course legal, cybersecurity, and regulatory risk disclosed in both filings: the 10-Q references Note 14 'Contingencies' for legal proceedings and states that 'damage amounts claimed in litigation against it are unreliable and unrelated to possible outcomes' (i.e., IBM cannot reliably estimate potential liability), while the 10-K's Risk Factors describe extensive cybersecurity threat exposure and the risk that 'goodwill or amortizable intangible assets may become impaired' given IBM's active acquisition strategy.

verdict.reasoning: The filing evidence shows a genuine, management-acknowledged Q2 FY2026 miss ('below our expectations') concentrated in the IBM Z mainframe/Infrastructure segment, with GAAP EPS down 1.7% year-over-year in the quarter [source: 2] - this is a real, filing-documented soft spot, not just market overreaction. But the broader picture is more constructive: H1 FY2026 revenue, net income, and EPS are all growing on a GAAP basis (+5.0%, +4.1%, +3.5% respectively), operating (non-GAAP) EPS grew faster still (+10.0% for H1), and Software - about 80% recurring revenue - grew a healthy 5.1% [source: 2]. Segment-level detail shows the weakness is genuinely isolated to Infrastructure/mainframe timing rather than broad-based deterioration [source: 2]. Confidence is medium rather than high because (a) I could not extract explicit forward guidance figures from the available text to confirm whether management has now lowered expectations further, and (b) elevated leverage (debt/equity 2.246) [source: 1] means further Infrastructure-segment softness would compound more than at a less-levered company.

sourcingNote: IBM's 10-K MD&A (Item 7) and much of Item 7A/Item 8 are incorporated by reference to IBM's separate 2025 Annual Report to Stockholders ('Refer to pages 6 through 38 of IBM's 2025 Annual Report...') rather than containing the actual analysis text within the 10-K document itself - so the 10-K's .mda content in this packet is boilerplate cross-reference language, not substantive MD&A, and was not cited for any factual claim above; all quantitative revenue/margin/earnings analysis instead relies on the Q2 FY2026 10-Q, which does contain full MD&A text, plus XBRL for the FY2025 annual figures. Of the 6 cached news headlines for IBM, only 'IBM Stock Options Price A Band Half Above Today's Price And A Third Below' was clearly and specifically about IBM; the others (an Accenture-focused piece, a Broadcom/Nutanix competitive piece mentioning IBM only in passing, a general quantum-stocks piece, a Monday.com piece, and a generic 'dow jones stocks moving' piece) were not IBM-specific enough to cite as sources for factual claims, so none of the cached news was used above - this is a real sourcing gap, not an oversight.
